claims.claim: Culling Game has no winner / not a tournament
claims.evidence: No victory condition; the game runs until players are dead and serves Kenjaku's ritual (Great Merger section; ch. 145 pp. 4-6, 11-12, ep. 50).

claims.claim: Camping can get you killed
claims.evidence: Rule 8: a score unchanged for 19 days = cursed technique removal, which Tengen confirms ends the player's life (ch. 146 pp. 4-5).

claims.claim: After Shibuya the story moves to the Culling Game
claims.evidence: The Culling Game immediately follows the Shibuya Incident.

claims.claim: Kenjaku absorbed Mahito
claims.evidence: Kenjaku absorbed Mahito with Cursed Spirit Manipulation at the end of Shibuya (ch. 136, ep. 47).

claims.claim: He used Mahito's Idle Transfiguration to activate people he had prepared for years
claims.evidence: Extracted Idle Transfiguration and remotely activated non-sorcerers he had marked (ch. 136).

claims.claim: Some ordinary humans awakened cursed techniques
claims.evidence: Second type: people who gained cursed techniques as new sorcerers (ch. 136).

claims.claim: Others became vessels for ancient sorcerers turned into cursed objects centuries ago
claims.evidence: First type: vessels who ingested cursed objects, the remains of sorcerers Kenjaku contracted with over a thousand years ago (ch. 136).

claims.claim: Think Yuji and Sukuna
claims.evidence: The wiki compares the first type directly to Yuji Itadori (a vessel who ingested a cursed object).

claims.claim: Japan divided into ten colonies surrounded by barriers
claims.evidence: Ten barrier colonies connected by barriers in a line down Japan (Hokkaido excluded).

claims.claim: Kills generate cursed energy for Kenjaku's goal of merging humanity with Tengen
claims.evidence: Cursed energy generated inside the colonies feeds the ritual merging Tengen with the people of Japan (ch. 202 pp. 12-17). Script says 'humanity'; canon says the people of Japan (Kenjaku's aim is to evolve humanity).

claims.claim: There are eight original rules
claims.evidence: Original rules 1-8.

claims.claim: Awakened players have 19 days to declare participation
claims.evidence: Rule 1.

claims.claim: Refusing = cursed technique removal, which can kill you
claims.evidence: Rule 2; Tengen confirms removal would end the player's life (ch. 146 pp. 4-5).

claims.claim: Walking into a colony makes you a player
claims.evidence: Rule 3.

claims.claim: Kogane is a shikigami that works like the game interface
claims.evidence: Shikigami known as Kogane serve as the game interface (ch. 146 pp. 2-8).

claims.claim: Kogane explains rules, tracks points, announces updates
claims.evidence: Kogane gives the rules/messages, shows player info and points (rule 9) and announces added rules (ch. 158).

claims.claim: Points are earned by killing other players
claims.evidence: Rule 4.

claims.claim: Sorcerer generally 5 points; non-sorcerer 1
claims.evidence: Rule 5 ('as a general rule').

claims.claim: 100 points can be spent to propose a new rule
claims.evidence: Rule 6.

claims.claim: Existing rules can't be deleted
claims.evidence: Rules cannot be subtracted (ch. 146 p. 8).

claims.claim: Game master can reject rules that seriously interfere with the game's continuation
claims.evidence: Rule 7: the game master must accept a new rule as long as it doesn't have a long-lasting effect on the game. On screen the card uses the canon wording 'long-lasting effect'.

claims.claim: Score unchanged for 19 days = technique can be removed
claims.evidence: Rule 8.

claims.claim: You can't win by being the last person alive
claims.evidence: There is no win condition in the rules; the game exists for the ritual.

claims.claim: Every battle helps fuel Kenjaku's ritual
claims.evidence: Cursed energy from deaths in the colonies fills the ritual (ch. 202, 209-210).

claims.claim: Yuji and Megumi get involved because of Tsumiki
claims.evidence: Megumi learns his sister is ensnared; he and Yuji form a plan to rescue her (ch. 144-146).

claims.claim: They try to save her without killing innocent people
claims.evidence: Plan: pressure a 100-point player to add rules so they can avoid killing people (ch. 158).

claims.claim: With Higuruma's help a rule allowing point transfers is added
claims.evidence: Rule 10, added by Hiromi Higuruma with 100 points (ch. 167 p. 1).

claims.claim: Transfers let you keep your score changing without killing
claims.evidence: Offsetting rule 8 by exchanging points was the stated plan (ch. 158).

claims.claim: It doesn't end the ritual
claims.evidence: The merger could only be stopped later; rule 10 doesn't end the game.

claims.claim: You can't simply cancel the game; a new rule must be accepted
claims.evidence: Rules can't be subtracted; rule 7 acceptance condition.

notes: Two wording notes, no factual errors: line 12 'humanity' vs canon 'people of Japan'; line 27 paraphrases rule 7 (screen shows canon wording).
Fortnite/Squid Game lines are analogies, not claims about JJK.
